subject: general
question:
Which of the following statements are correct in relation to the extraction of metals?

The metals which lie high in the reactivity series are extracted by the electrolysis of molten ore.

The metals of medium reactivity series exist as sulphides and carbonates in nature.

It is easier to extract a metal from its sulphide in comparison to oxides.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only a and b**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The extraction of metals depends on their position in the **reactivity series**. Metals at the top of the series, such as **Potassium (K)**, **Sodium (Na)**, **Calcium (Ca)**, **Magnesium (Mg)**, and **Aluminium (Al)**, are highly reactive and cannot be reduced by **carbon** because their affinity for oxygen is higher than that of carbon. These metals are extracted by the **electrolysis** of their **molten ores** (usually chlorides or oxides). ***Hence, statement a is correct.***
 
• Metals located in the middle of the **reactivity series**, such as **Iron (Fe)**, **Zinc (Zn)**, and **Lead (Pb)**, are moderately reactive. In nature, these metals are predominantly found as **sulphides** or **carbonates** rather than pure oxides or free elements. ***Hence, statement b is correct.***
